answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 55% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the attacker's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the bridge reward in the hollow ledger costs the operator directly, and the whisper audit records each payout. A farm of 94 keys hence funds the parties working against it, so growing the army of identities makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
